articles.title: Immediate danger recognition
articles.summary: Field planning and documentation checklist for immediate danger recognition. This is a preliminary administrative guide, not a verified technical procedure.
body: Begin by identifying immediate threats and following current official emergency instructions. Do not enter a hazardous area to complete paperwork or retrieve equipment.
Define the purpose of immediate danger recognition in one sentence, including who will use the record or procedure.
Identify the responsible person and a backup; record their contact method if appropriate.
Inspect the relevant equipment, supplies, or information for missing, damaged, expired, or outdated items.
Record the current condition, location, date, and any immediate limitations using a paper or local offline record.
Flag urgent safety concerns and refer them to qualified personnel or current official guidance before proceeding.
Prepare an accessible printed copy or labeled kit for use during a power or communications outage.
Agree on a trigger for using this procedure and a fallback if the preferred option is unavailable.
Test the procedure in a safe practice setting; record failures and correct them before an emergency.
Set a review interval and update the record whenever equipment, contacts, or circumstances change.
At handoff, tell the next person what was checked, what remains unresolved, and where the current record is stored.
